newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end higher on fresh buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end higher on fresh buying.

text.p: Jakarta shares prices closed up on Friday but profit-taking pulled them off their highs for the day, brokers said.
They said the market had received a boost from locally-led speculative buying in some secondaries coupled with positive sentiment from Thursday's sharp rise in New York.
The composite index rose 4.21 points, or 0.67 percent, to 632.52 points after touching a high of 635.35.
Brokers and analysts said the market was likely to be mixed on Monday with some investors sidelined as the Christmas holiday approached.
"Volume-wise, trading will be quieter. But the index could stay on the positive side on speculative buying," an analyst in a local firm said.
Brokers said retail and consumer counters Matahari Putra Prima and Multipolar could remain a focus for the market in the coming week on speculation they were discussing an alliance.
Neither company has commented on the market talk.
Multipolar rose 25 rupiah to 1,675 on 13 million shares after earlier rising to 1,750 rupiah. Matahari was down 175 rupiah to 2,725 on 1.6 million shares.
Hero Supermarket and Mayora Indah also traded actively on fresh buying, brokers said.

"Besides all the rumours, the retail and consumer sectors seem promising in 1997 with consumer spending likely to rise following the downtrend in interest rates and stable economic growth," an analyst from a Korean firm said.
Brokers said there was only limited market reaction to a presidential decree ordering wealthy individuals and companies to donate two percent of their profits to the poor.

"We had already heard about it two weeks ago but it is still not clear. I think the market shrugged off the news today as it enjoyed positive sentiment from Wall Street," an analyst from a Singapore-based firm said.
